claims.text: The starting protective coating is an FCC/BCC dual-phase high-entropy alloy.
The starting coating has a baseline level of interphase-boundary coherence and lattice distortion.
A tailored heat treatment can enhance interphase-boundary coherence.
A tailored heat treatment can increase localized lattice distortions.
Coherent interphase boundaries promote localized stress fields.
Coherent interphase boundaries intensify localized lattice distortions.
Localized stress fields and lattice distortions hinder dislocation motion.
Localized stress fields and lattice distortions particularly hinder dislocation climb.
Hindering dislocation motion reduces progressive plastic deformation and slows creep.
The enhanced heat treatment will produce a lower creep strain rate than the conventional treatment under identical sustained stress conditions.
The enhanced heat treatment will delay the onset of plastic deformation relative to the baseline.
The conventional-treatment baseline has fewer coherent interphase boundaries than the proposed treated coating.
The conventional-treatment baseline has lower lattice distortion than the proposed treated coating.
The proposed mechanism applies at intermediate temperatures where diffusion and dislocation climb contribute significantly to creep.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to conditions below those causing microstructural instability such as recrystallization.
The relative contributions of lattice distortion and interphase-boundary coherence to creep resistance are unresolved.
The creep-resistance effect may depend on the precise alloy composition.
